# Godwill Zulu

::: {.about-tagline}
PhD Researcher in Statistics, Trinity College Dublin · Bayesian Evaluation · Generative AI in Higher Education
:::
:::

Did it work, for whom, and how sure can we be? As a PhD researcher in Statistics at Trinity College Dublin, I ask those questions about generative AI in higher education.

I started in monitoring and evaluation in Zimbabwe, with a first-class degree in Operations Research and Statistics, designing M&E systems and baseline studies for community health, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), and young people's sexual and reproductive health programmes. That work taught me that an evaluation is only as good as its data and its design: how outcomes are measured, who gets counted, and what a comparison can and cannot tell you.

My MSc in Health Data Science at the University of Galway specialised in Bayesian hierarchical modelling, with a thesis on spatio-temporal small area estimation of under-five malaria prevalence in West Africa. During a co-op with Eli Lilly's Competitive Intelligence Statistics team, I curated and quality-checked clinical trial efficacy data.

My PhD uses Bayesian methods to evaluate how students' use of generative AI affects their learning and assessment. It moves from a scoping review, to observational studies linking self-reported AI use with learning-platform and assessment data, and, where feasible, to randomised experiments. The problems are the ones I met in the field: exposure that is hard to measure, confounding, and outcomes observed over short windows.

## What you'll find here

- **[Articles](archive.qmd):** the statistical foundations beneath machine learning, from random variables to likelihood. Intuition first, then the mathematics, then something you can actually use.
- **[Notes](notes.qmd):** shorter, more personal writing on AI, learning, and higher education.

## What I'm working on

**PhD, Trinity College Dublin:** Bayesian evaluation of how students' use of generative AI affects their learning and assessment.

**Bayesian Explorer:** An interactive Shiny app I built to help students develop intuition for Bayesian inference. Visualises prior-likelihood-posterior relationships in real time. [Try it here →](https://ckisxn-godwill-zulu.shinyapps.io/bayesian-explorer/)

## Tools

R, Stan and JAGS for Bayesian modelling; Shiny and Quarto for interactive tools and writing; Python for machine learning workflows.

My approach: principles first, tools second. The foundations don't just make you better at statistics. They make you harder to fool.
